title: The Better Angels Of Our Nature

questions.q: Why are ideologies especially prone to violence?
a: They claim to serve huge groups and a greater good
They are usually led by unstable individuals
They reject all forms of government
They spread fastest among soldiers
questions.why: Lesson 1 says ideologies recruit large groups and justify violence in the name of a higher cause.

questions.q: What does the Flynn effect describe?
a: A steady rise in IQ scores of about three points per decade
The decline of violence after each major war
The spread of literacy through printing
The tendency of groups to become more extreme
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines the Flynn effect as the continuous rise in measured intelligence over time.

questions.q: How does greater reasoning reduce violence?
a: It debunks superstitious justifications and encourages impartial thinking
It makes people physically healthier and calmer
It replaces religion with stronger laws
It discourages people from joining groups
questions.why: Lesson 2 says reason undermines superstition and helps people act for the common good.

questions.q: What role does the printing press play in Pinker's account?
a: It let humanitarian philosophy spread and reduce violence
It gave governments better maps for war
It replaced spoken language with written law
It made weapons cheaper to produce
questions.why: Lesson 3 says print allowed humanist ideas to spread and displace superstitious killings.

questions.q: How were criminals treated as humanism spread?
a: With dignity, which reduced violence in law and punishment
They were exiled rather than imprisoned
They were handed to religious courts
They were forced into military service
questions.why: Lesson 3 says humanism extended dignity even to criminals, removing violence from law and order.
